title: THE LIST THAT SHOWS OUR NEED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'"No man who has any defect may come near: no man who is blind or
lame, disfigured or deformed; no man with a crippled foot or hand, or
who is a hunchback or a dwarf, or who has any eye defect, or who has
festering or running sores or damaged testicles"'" - Lev 21:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This detailed list can feel uncomfortable to read. It names real human
conditions, many of which people still live with today. We must not
soften the difficulty, but we must read it in its place.

The list is not a ranking of human worth. It is a description of a
system that demanded perfection at every point - and could never
supply it. Even the priests themselves were sinners who had to offer
sacrifices for their own sin before serving others (Heb 7:27).

That is the point the whole old system was quietly making. Nobody
measured up. Not the animals for long. Not the priests. Not the
people. The system kept saying, "not yet, not him, not this one."

Then Jesus came. And look at who He touched: the blind, the lame, the
man with the withered hand, the leper. He did not merely permit them
near - He went to them. In Him, Isaiah's promise came alive: the blind
see, the lame walk (Matt 11:5).

Dear friend, whatever weakness you carry in your body or your history,
it is not a barrier to Christ. He specialises in the very people the
old system excluded.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What weakness makes me feel disqualified before God?
2. How does Jesus' treatment of the excluded change my view of Him?
3. Who might feel unwelcome around me, and how can I change that?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, thank You that You come near to the very people others
push away. Come near to me in my weakness and use me to welcome
others. Amen.
